summary: Read-only: 5 independent options-strategy designs for a ~$97 Robinhood account (live chain pricing), judged by 3 lenses, synthesized into one pre-registered plan

designs.name: D1 'Overnight Call Sprint' (OCS): all-in NVDA weekly calls bought at 15:51 and sold at 09:31, Mon-Thu nights only, with a hard stop at $200, a soft floor at $80 and a 20-night cap
designs.one_line: Replace NVDL with one NVDA call (11-17 DTE, the deepest strike the account can afford) on Mon-Thu nights to get about 25x NVDA exposure. Verdict: the overnight edge does NOT survive options costs at a $97 account. This is a lottery ticket: about 14-17% chance of reaching $200 within 3 months, about 28% chance of hitting the $50 KILL, median about $73. The NVDL engine is the better bet over 12 months (P(>=200) 20% vs 18%, P(<=50) 7% vs 40%).
designs.options_level_needed: Level 2 only (buying calls). No spreads (Level 3) are needed. Call debit spreads were checked and rejected: a 2-leg overnight round trip costs about 16% of the debit in spreads (e.g. 11/6 230/240C, 0.78-0.87 net, quoted 6 to 9 cents wide). NVDL options were also rejected: 10/30 33C bid 0.65 / ask 0.79, 34C 0.38/0.54, 32C 0.89/1.27, i.e. 20-40% wide. The human must enable Level 2 options on account 8334 only (the agent cannot apply).
designs.l2_fallback: The design is already Level-2-only, so approval of L2 alone is enough. If options are NOT approved, or the human does not accept the risk statement below, keep the current NVDL engine (RULES_v3 §3-§6) unchanged. By these numbers that is also the recommended choice. NVDL BASE: 12-month P(>=200) 20% at period end and 29% touched at any point, P(<=50) 7%, median $133, E[log] +0.59% per week. D1 BASE: 12-month 18% at end / 22% touched, P(<=50) 40%, median $85. The options sprint beats NVDL on P(200) only if the overnight edge is half-strength or gone. In that case NVDL is about 1-6% and D1 about 5-10%, but D1 carries a 54-69% chance of ending <= $50. Re-open condition for using options as leverage (not as a lottery): equity large enough that one ~0.30-delta, 2-week NVDA call (~$300-450 today) is <= 15% of E, i.e. E >= ~$2,000-3,000. Then a Kelly-sized overlay becomes possible, and it must still show positive executed P&L on the shadow log. Side observation, NOT adopted: NVDA weekend nights averaged -3.6bp vs weekday +18.5bp (2017-2026, difference t=2.2). The sign flips in 2015-18 (sub-period t -0.6 to +1.6), so it is too fragile to change the Friday NVDL hold; it is noted for the 2027-01-11 review only.
designs.rules:
OCS v0. Every step is executable with the existing wakes (07:45, 09:26->09:31:05 bridge, 15:48->15:51 bridge, 8-minute loop).

0) GATES before the first real order.
(a) The human enables Options Level 2 on 8334 and nothing on 3273.
(b) The human explicitly accepts this risk statement: "~1 in 6 chance of $200 within 3 months; ~1 in 3 chance of the $50 KILL; a flat NVDA night costs ~11% of equity; a -2% NVDA night costs ~48%."
(c) SHADOW phase, at least 5 Mon-Thu nights (it can start tomorrow, needs no approval, places no orders). Each night: pick the contract with rule 3-4 at 15:50. Log bid/ask at 15:51 and at 09:25, 09:31:05, 09:33, 09:36 and 09:40 the next morning. Compute k = median(exit half-spread at 09:31-09:36) / (15:51 half-spread).
ABORT the design (stay on NVDL) if k > 3, or if mean shadow executed return (15:51 ask -> 09:33 bid) < -5%/night over the shadow nights.

1) SPRINT NIGHTS. Only Mon-Thu regular sessions where the next session is the next calendar day. NOT on:
- Fridays;
- pre-holiday nights (e.g. Wed 11/25);
- half-days (11/27, 12/24);
- the NVDA earnings night (entry 11/17, report after the close, verified by get_earnings_results).
Also not on any night when §6 PAUSE is active. On every non-sprint night the existing NVDL engine runs exactly as in RULES_v3 §3-§5: NVDL first, NVDX filler, cash on the 11/17 night.

2) INSTRUMENT. NVDA standard calls only. Never NVDL/NVDX options, puts, spreads or short options. Long premium only, so the maximum loss is the premium paid.

3) EXPIRY. Among the listed NVDA expirations (get_option_chains), take the one whose calendar DTE from the entry date is in [11,17], closest to 14 (ties go to the longer one). If that expiry is on or after the NVDA earnings date (2026-11-17), use instead the latest expiry strictly before the earnings date, provided its DTE is >= 5. Otherwise it is not a sprint night (run NVDL).

4) STRIKE AND SIZE (computed at 15:50:00 from get_option_quotes).
- E = account total (all cash at this time; the NVDL leg was sold at 09:31). B = 0.95*E.
- cost(K) = ask*100 + 0.04 (fees). K35 = the strike with delta closest to 0.35 and delta <= 0.40.
- If cost(K35) <= B: buy N = floor(B/cost(K35)) contracts of K35.
- Else buy N = 1 of the LOWEST strike K >= ATM with cost(K) <= B, delta >= 0.05, bid > 0, and (ask - bid) <= max(0.05, 0.10*mid).
- If no strike qualifies, it is not a sprint night (run NVDL).
- Leftover cash stays as cash overnight.

5) ENTRY ORDERS. Limit orders, GFD, with INV-12 intent logged first.
- 15:51:00: buy at min(ask, mid + 0.01), rounded to tick (0.01 below $3, 0.05 at or above $3).
- 15:53:00 unfilled: re-price to ask.
- 15:56:00 unfilled: re-price to ask + one tick.
- 15:58:00 unfilled: cancel, VERIFY cancelled, then immediately run the NVDL entry (limit at ask + 0.15%), and only if it is still before 15:59:00.
- Partial fills are kept and are never sold the same day.

6) EXIT ORDERS (next session).
- 09:31:05: sell all at max(bid, mid - 0.01).
- 09:32:30: bid + 0.01 if the spread is >= 0.03, else bid.
- 09:34:00: bid.
- 09:36:00: bid - 0.01.
- 09:40:00: max(0.01, bid - 0.05).
- 09:45 and every 2 minutes after: bid - 10%, until filled.
Never hold intentionally past 10:00. A late wake exits immediately (same logic as §5).

7) SPRINT TERMINATION. Evaluated after every exit fill and at EOD; all are permanent until a new human OK.
- SUCCESS: account total >= $200. Stop options and return to the NVDL engine.
- SOFT FLOOR: account total < $80 after any exit. Stop options and return to the NVDL engine.
- TIME STOP: 20 sprint nights used.
- KILL (§6, unchanged): total <= $50. Flatten, HALT, alert the human.
- Earnings window: no sprint entries on 11/17. The sprint resumes 11/18 only if no termination has fired.

8) PDT. Options are opened at 15:51 and closed the next session only. Never close an option on the day it was opened, even on adverse news after 15:51. Day trades used: 0.

9) IDLE CASH. Daytime 09:31-15:51: cash, as now (the day leg stays suspended).

10) RECORDS.
- trades.csv exit_kind "ocs" with the OCC symbol, delta at entry, entry ask/mid, exit bid/mid, NVDA 15:51 and 09:31 prices.
- orders.jsonl INV-12.
- A shadow/fill-cost line every night.
- Post-mortem when the sprint ends.

11) WHAT IS UNCHANGED. Account 8334 only. Never 3273. No transfers. KILL and PAUSE levels. NVDL engine on all non-sprint nights. Edge-decay switch §3(f): if it fires, no sprint nights either.

designs.simulation:
METHOD
- NVDA close->open returns, 2017-01 to 2026-10-16, with NVDA earnings nights removed (from research/edge_decay/overnight_thru_20261016.csv): weekday nights n=1885, mean +18.5bp, sd 1.545%; weekend nights n=510, mean -3.6bp. Weekday and weekend pools are bootstrapped separately.
- Each simulated year has 252 nights: Mon-Thu sprint-eligible, Fri night NVDL, and every 63rd night cash for earnings.
- Option pricing: Black-Scholes in calendar time with r=4%, using the CURRENT 10/22 smile fitted to the 10/30 and 11/6 calls. The model reproduces the quotes (e.g. 11/6 232.5C model mid 0.88 vs observed 0.85; 10/30 225C 0.90 vs 0.94).
- Overnight IV path: dIV = a + b*r + e. It was calibrated on real 10-minute NVDA option bars (93 contracts, 978 contract-nights, Jul 27 to Oct 22 2026; entry 15:50, exit ~09:40; NVDA 5-minute bars at matching times). Result for 5-16 DTE, delta .08-.40 weekday nights: a = +0.62 vol-pt (night-clustered se 0.14; only +0.17 in October), b = -0.10, residual sd 1.1pt.
- Execution: buy at ask = mid + hs, where hs(P) = 0.01 + 0.012P fitted to the 10/22 close quotes; sell at bid = mid - k*hs; fee $0.04 per contract per side.
- 40k paths, KILL at $50 is absorbing. Scripts are s01-s09.

SCENARIOS
- BASE: half the IV pop (+0.32pt), k=2.
- CONS: no IV pop.
- OPT: full pop, k=1.
- VOL26: overnight sd scaled to 1.30%.
- HALF and ZERO: the overnight edge halved or demeaned.
- HOT: +15bp per weekday night, like Aug-Oct 2026.

designs.edge_basis:
The underlying edge is real but small: NVDA weekday close->open averaged +18.5bp (t ~5.2, 2017-2026, ex-earnings); the all-night mean is +12.1bp (t 4.1); the 2025-26 subsample has t 1.4-1.7. Options do not create edge. They rescale the drift by about 25-36x per dollar of premium and add three frictions.

1) Bid/ask. About 2-5% of premium per side at the close, assumed about 2x that at the open. That is about 7% of premium per round trip, roughly $6 per night on the first-trade contract.

2) Theta vs gamma (the variance risk premium).
- Theta: -$7.6 per night at constant IV.
- Offsets: gamma gives back about $5-7 at 1.3-1.55% overnight sd; the open IV re-mark gives back about +$2.6 in BASE.

3) Leverage far beyond Kelly.
- Even with the full historical edge, the growth-optimal NVDA exposure is about 5-8x. One affordable contract is 25-36x.
- In the most favourable case (OPT) the Kelly fraction is about 13% of equity, about $13. That is below the cost of any contract with delta >= 0.05 (about $30 or more).
- So the position cannot be sized rationally at $97, and E[log] is about -7% to -14% per option night.

Net: the drift adds about +$4.6 per night on the first-trade contract and the frictions take about $6-11. The executed mean is about 0 (BASE) and the median about -7%. A flat night costs 11% of equity.

Evidence quality.
- Underlying returns: strong (2,395 nights).
- Option behaviour: one regime only (62 nights of 10-minute bars, Jul-Oct 2026; the IV pop shrank in October).
- Open spreads: unmeasured, hence the shadow gate.
- Conclusion: the edge does not survive. D1 is a lottery whose payoff depends almost entirely on the NVDA regime during the 2-4 nights it typically lasts.
risks: Single-night gap: an NVDA -2% night (4.7% of weekday nights are <= -2.5%) costs ~48% of equity; -4% costs ~70%. No stop-loss works because options do not trade overnight. The soft floor cannot prevent a one-night drop from $97 to below $50: P(<=50) is about 28% within 3 months.
Time decay and spread: a flat NVDA night costs ~$11 (11% of E). The break-even overnight move is +0.49%, which happened on only 40% of weekday nights.
The open spread is unmeasured. Going from 1x to 3x the close spread moves the per-night EV from +2.3% to -2.5%. Mitigation: the shadow gate (rule 0c) and stepped limit exits.

Model risk: the IV re-mark at the open (+0.62pt) comes from 49 weekday nights in one regime and fell to +0.17pt in October. With no IV pop (CONS), the 12-month P(>=200) falls to 15-19% and P(<=50) rises to 42%.
Regime dependence: the 3-month replay looked great (97 -> 240, peak 632) only because NVDA ran +33bp per night. In ZERO/HALF-edge regimes D1 ends at or below $50 54-69% of the time.
It does not dominate the baseline. Over 12 months P(>=200) is equal or lower (18-24% vs 20%) and ruin is 5-6x higher. Its only advantage is speed: about 14-17% within 3 months vs about 0%.
Behavioural/process risk: the temptation to continue after SUCCESS or to re-enter after the floor fires. The rules make both permanent until a new human OK.

Operational: a missed 09:31 exit means holding an OTM call intraday (theta plus possible downside). A missed 15:51 entry falls back to NVDL. Partial fills cannot be unwound the same day (PDT rule). Robinhood penny/nickel ticks at $3.

Earnings and calendar: expiries straddling 11/17 carry earnings IV, so the rule forces pre-earnings expiries and skips 11/17. Monday/Wednesday NVDA expiry listings may change. Holiday gaps are excluded.
Approval risk: Level 2 may be delayed or denied, and only the human can enable it. The agent must never touch account 3273.
designs.ops_feasibility:
PDT: zero day trades. Buy at 15:51, sell the next session after 09:31. Rule 8 forbids same-day closes, including partial fills.

Wakes: fit the current schedule.
- 15:48 ENTRY wake: bridge to 15:50:00, read get_option_chains, get_option_instruments and get_option_quotes (2-3 calls, about 20s), place at 15:51:00, re-price at 15:53 and 15:56, cancel at 15:58 with fallback to NVDL by 15:59.
- 09:26 EXIT wake: bridge to 09:31:05, then the stepped limits to 09:40 and beyond (the loop is already in turn).
- Fridays and non-sprint nights: unchanged NVDL flow.

Liquidity at our size: 1 contract against open interest of 685-58,000 and daily volume of 1,000-140,000 on these strikes. Fills at the ask are certain; fills at the mid are uncertain. Quoted size of 1-200 contracts is adequate.

Spreads: 1-5 cents at the close on $0.2-5 NVDA weeklies. At the open they are unknown and assumed about 2x; the shadow log measures them before any money is risked. NVDL options (20-40% wide) are unusable.

Account: limited_margin, so settlement is not a constraint. Options require Level 2 and the human must enable it. Robinhood options orders are limit, GFD, regular hours only (no extended-hours option trading, per the chain's extended_hours_state=disabled). Fees are about $0.03-0.05 per contract per side.

Overnight: no reaction is possible and none is planned. Risk is capped only by the premium, which is all of equity on sprint nights.

Data: 1-minute option bars exist for recent weeks (10-minute bars back to at least late July), so nightly shadow and fill-cost logging is feasible.

designs.name: CCX-1: NVDA earnings call-spread overlay on the overnight NVDA-2x engine (catalyst convexity)
designs.one_line: Keep the NVDL/NVDX 15:52 to 09:31 engine on every ordinary night. On each NVDA earnings night (first one Tue 11/17), put about 25% of equity into one NVDA weekly call spread, 2.5 wide and about 8% out of the money: buy 15:35 on report day, sell 09:40 next morning. In my planning case this lifts P(reach $200 within 12 months) from about 27% to about 38%, and raises P(end at or below $50) from 7% to 21%. Its edge rests entirely on NVDA's historical post-earnings up-gap continuing.
designs.options_level_needed: Level 3: vertical debit spreads, sent as one 2-leg combo order. Account 8334 is limited margin, so it can apply for Level 3. It should apply now: the first event is 11/17, about 18 sessions away. If Level 3 is not in place by Mon 11/16, skip 11/17; there is no substitute event. No margin borrowing is used: every position is a debit, defined-risk and paid from cash.
designs.l2_fallback:
With Level 2 only (no spreads), replace the spread with ONE single long NVDA call. Same expiry, same entry (15:35 on E) and exit (09:40 on E+1). Budget B = min(0.25*E, E-60). Strike K = the lowest listed strike >= 1.06*S whose mid+0.03 <= B/100; skip if there is none at or below 1.16*S. At E=97 that is about a 235C-240C (+11 to +13% out of the money), costing about $0.13-0.28 on 11/17 by model.

Simulated, 40k paths, engine with edge:
- Planning case (+1% drift): 12-month P(>=200) 22.2% (touched 26.9%), P(<=50) 26.1%, median $80, log growth +0.52%/week.
- No-edge-in-options case: P(>=200) 11.4%, P(<=50) 31.5%, -0.15%/week.
So it is worse than the Level 3 version, and model-fragile: my smile model underprices today's far right-wing calls (270C market 0.205 vs model 0.127).

Honest note: a non-option alternative beats it on risk in every engine-edge scenario. That alternative is holding NVDL on the earnings night with 50% of E, which lifts the RULES_v3 §3(d) blackout for half the size and sells at 09:31. Its 12-month results with the engine edge: P(>=200) 18.5-26% (touched 28-37%), P(<=50) 5.7-8%, log growth +0.52 to +0.77%/week. With no engine edge it fails like the baseline: P(>=200) 1.4-2.8%, P(<=50) 28-36%. If only Level 2 arrives, I recommend asking the human to choose between the single-call lottery ticket and this NVDL-night variant.
designs.rules:
R0 SCOPE
- Trade only account 445788334 (8334). Never touch account 3273. No transfers.
- Limit or combo-limit orders only, never market orders for options.
- Every order gets an INV-12 intent line listing both legs.

R1 BASE ENGINE (unchanged, RULES_v3 §3-§8)
- Every non-event night: NVDL first, then NVDX filler, up to 0.98*E. Buy 15:52, sell 09:31. Cash intraday.
- KILL stays absolute: E <= 50 means flatten, HALT, alert the human.
- PAUSE change: a realized overlay loss is pre-budgeted, so it does not feed PAUSE. On E+1, after the spread is closed, the PAUSE 20-session high restarts from the post-event equity. Engine losses still trigger PAUSE as before.

R2 EVENT SET
- Only NVDA's own scheduled after-close earnings:
  - Tue 2026-11-17 (Robinhood: pm, verified).
  - ~Wed 2027-02-24 (unverified).
  - ~late May 2027 and ~late Aug 2027 (estimated).
- Verify each date with get_earnings_results 15 business days before and again on the morning of E. If it is not verified pm by E morning, skip.
- Not traded, with reasons:
  - AMD 11/3: last 8 gaps mean -4.5%, no directional prior. Implied event sd ~7.2% vs realized rms ~8.6%, so no vol edge. 11/04 weekly ATM markets are 12-14% wide.
  - FOMC 10/28: decision is intraday; a same-day round trip would be a PDT day trade.
  - MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META nights: PEER-NIGHTS-20261022 found no mean effect.

R3 INSTRUMENT
- NVDA call vertical debit spread: long K1 call, short K2 call, K2 = next listed strike above K1. Width is 2.5, or 5 where 2.5 strikes are not listed (above 240 today).
- Expiry = first listed NVDA expiration after the report: 2026-11-20 for the 11/17 event; the Friday weekly after each later report.

R4 BUDGET
- E = broker total at 15:30 on E. The account is all cash then: the engine sold at 09:31 and does not re-enter that night.
- B = min(0.25*E, E-60) dollars.
- Once E >= 200 (target reached; alert the human): B = min(0.10*E, E-150).
- If B < $10, skip the event. The overlay therefore switches itself off below E ≈ $70.

R5 STRIKE SELECTION (15:30-15:35 ET on E; S = NVDA last)
- Candidates: listed K1 with 1.035*S <= K1 <= 1.10*S, ascending.
- For each candidate:
  - combo mid m = mid(K1 call) - mid(K2 call)
  - combo natural nat = ask(K1) - bid(K2)
  - n = min(3, floor(B / (100*(m+0.03))))
- Take the first (nearest-to-money) K1 with n >= 1.
- Skip the event if:
  - no candidate has n >= 1;
  - nat - m > 0.06 (illiquid);
  - the ATM straddle for that expiry costs more than 9% of S (event priced too rich).

R6 ENTRY (on E)

designs.edge_basis:
The edge has one source: NVDA's after-close earnings reports have produced a positive opening gap on average.
- All 47 reports 2015-2026: mean +3.20%, median +2.83%, t 3.0.
- The mean is stable by sub-period: 2015-19 +3.4%, 2020-26 +3.1%, last 12 +3.0%, last 8 +2.6%.
- The calls are priced roughly symmetrically around the forward: today's chain prices the event at 5.73% sd with a negative call skew.
- A call debit spread about 8% out of the money therefore buys the right tail cheaply if the drift persists.
- The long-run realized gap rms (7.9%) also exceeds the implied 5.7%, which helps out-of-the-money strikes.

Evidence quality is weak to moderate:
- (1) Selection and hindsight bias. NVDA was the decade's best megacap, and its 47 earnings nights carry about 20% of its 11-year log return. The academic earnings-announcement premium for typical stocks is tens of bp, not +3%.
- (2) The recent realized gap distribution is narrower than implied: last-12 rms 5.2% vs 5.7%. Recent gaps also faded intraday (last 8: next-day open->close mean -3.4%), which is why we exit at 09:40.
- (3) Options carry a volatility risk premium. With zero drift and implied-matching vol (FAIR), each bet loses about 24% of the debit on average, and -13% log growth per event at this size.
- (4) There are only 4 events a year, so live results will not confirm or refute anything for years.

The planning case (+1% drift) gives a positive arithmetic EV per bet (+41% of debit). The bet is sized about 3x Kelly to buy probability of reaching $200, so expected log growth is about equal to or slightly below the baseline engine. The baseline itself is the second uncertain edge: NVDA overnight drift, t ≈ 1-2.7 depending on window.
risks: Most likely outcome of each event is a near-total loss of the debit: P(lose >=90%) is 50-71% across scenarios. After one loss E drops to about $74, PAUSE-like psychology sets in, and the next event is often unaffordable (B < $10 or nothing within +10% out of the money), so the overlay is effectively 1-2 shots per year.

The drift assumption may be pure hindsight. If NVDA's earnings gap drift is 0 (MU0/FAIR), the overlay lowers log growth (-0.10 to +0.12%/week vs +0.54%) and P(<=50) at 12 months rises to 25-28% even with the engine edge, or 61% without it.

Model risk: no real option backtest exists, because Robinhood has no expired-contract history. Entry IV on 11/17 may imply a larger move than today's 5.7% (NVDA earnings straddles were often 6-8%). At 6.5% sd, 12-month P(>=200) falls from 29.6% to 22.4%. At 7.5% the bets become unaffordable and are skipped.
Granularity: at E ≈ $97 the bet is exactly 1 contract, so sizing jumps in steps. The strike is set by the budget (about +8% out of the money), not by an optimum.
Strike availability: above 240 NVDA lists only $5 strikes. If NVDA rallies before 11/17, the only spreads may be 5-wide, which can be unaffordable, so the event is skipped.

Execution: opening option quotes on E+1 are wide. A rest-and-walk exit can give up 0.05-0.10 per combo. Partial fills or leg risk exist if the broker ever splits a combo (never leg manually). At 0.06 slippage, 12-month P(>=200) is 24.8% and log growth +0.28%/week.
Short-call assignment or pin risk if a spread is left open into expiry with the short strike near the money. R7 forces a close by Fri 15:00. Robinhood sellout is 15:30 ET.
Options approval: Level 3 may not be granted, or not before 11/16. The Level 2 single-call fallback is worse and model-fragile.
PAUSE interaction: the R1 change exempts overlay losses from PAUSE. That is a deliberate loosening of an existing risk rule and needs the human's OK.
The KILL boundary is protected by B <= E-60, but an engine gap of -20% (NVDL) the night after a lost bet could still take E from about 62 to about 50.
The baseline engine's own edge is uncertain (t ~1 on Feb-Oct 2026 executable prices). With no engine edge, every variant has P(<=50) of 44-61% at 12 months.
Earnings date change or pre-announcement: R2 verification on E morning; skip if the date is unverified.

designs.rules:
HARD RULES (unchanged): trade only account 445788334. Never touch account ending 3273. No transfers. KILL at E <= 50: flatten, halt, alert the human. Never sell naked options. Never use margin.

ENGINE (unchanged T3X v1.7):
- Buy at 15:52 ET: NVDL first, then NVDX filler, with 0.98 x the cash available at 15:52. Sell at 09:31:05.
- Flat on NVDA earnings nights (11/17/2026, then each report night; next estimated 2/24/2027).
- §3(f) edge-decay switch, §4/§5 limit logic and §6 PAUSE/KILL as in RULES_v3.
- Engine capital is all cash not spent on the sleeve. Whole-share sizing means that at E ≈ 97 with a $16 sleeve the engine holds 2 NVDL (about 64% of E) instead of 3.

SLEEVE:

S1 Budget
- E = broker total equity at decision time: cash, plus ETFs at bid, plus any spread at mid.
- Floor F = $80.00, fixed and not ratcheting.
- Per-cycle budget B = min(0.20 x E, E - 80).
- If B < $8, skip the cycle. In practice the sleeve is off whenever E < $88.

S2 Schedule
- First open: the first session after Level 3 approval, between 10:00 and 15:30 ET.
- After that, open on each roll date.
- Roll date: the first trading day on which the held spread's expiry is <= 25 calendar days away. Planned dates: 12/21/2026, 2/22/2027, 4/26/2027, 6/21/2027, 8/23/2027, 10/25/2027.
- If the sleeve is flat (already took profit, or skipped), the next open still waits for the scheduled roll date.

S3 Contract selection
- Expiry: the first standard 3rd-Friday NVDA monthly with >= 80 calendar days left. Approval by 10/26 gives 2027-01-15; approval 10/27-11/19 gives 2027-02-19.
- Structure: call debit spread, buy K1 and sell K2 = K1 + W.
- Width W = $10 while NVDA is 150-300. Otherwise W = the listed strike step closest to 4.7% of spot.
- Limit L = mid + 0.25 x (natural - mid), rounded up to $0.01.
  - mid = mid(K1) - mid(K2)
  - natural = ask(K1) - bid(K2)
- K1 = the lowest listed strike >= spot such that K2 is listed, 100L + $0.10 <= B, and W/L >= 4.
- Quantity n = floor(B / (100L + 0.10)), which is 1 until E ≈ $190.
- If nothing qualifies, skip the cycle.

S4 Entry order
- One 2-leg limit order, day order: buy-to-open K1, sell-to-open K2.
- Window: 10:00-15:30 ET only. Nothing in the first 30 minutes. Nothing after 15:30, because the 15:48-15:58 engine entry has priority.
- On each ≤9-minute loop scan, re-quote and raise the limit by $0.01, never above min(natural, (B - 0.10)/100).
- At 15:30, cancel. Retry the next session from S3 with fresh quotes.
- After 3 failed sessions, skip to the next roll date.
- After a fill, verify 0 open orders (INV-9).

S5 Exits
- (a) Take-profit: starting the session after the open, on each scan compute the closing natural credit C = bid(K1) - ask(K2).
  - If 100 x n x C >= 3 x total debit paid including fees, sell-to-close as one 2-leg limit at mid - 0.25 x (mid - C).
  - Step the limit down $0.01 per scan, but not below C.
  - Never close a spread on the day it was opened (PDT).
- (b) Roll: on the roll date, sell-to-close with the same limit logic, then open the next cycle the same day.
  - Exception: if bid(K1) < $0.02 and both strikes are more than 5% out of the money, let the spread expire worthless.
- (c) KILL: if E <= 50, close the spread at natural and run the existing §6 flatten.
- (d) No stop-loss. Never add to, roll up or leg out of a spread.

S6 Skim and rebalance
- All sleeve proceeds go to cash and are used automatically by the next 15:52 engine entry.
- The sleeve is re-funded only at roll dates, through S1.
- Profits above the floor are recycled at no more than 20% of E per cycle.

S7 Pause and stop
- No new sleeve while §3(f) has the engine in cash, while PAUSE is active, or while trader/HUMAN_STOP exists.
- The PAUSE high-water is computed with the open spread valued at cost, not at its mark.
- KILL at 50 is unchanged.

S8 Events
- No sleeve blackout for earnings or FOMC. The Jan-15 spread spans the 11/17 NVDA report; the event premium is in the price.

METHOD

Data
- NVDA daily OHLC 2015-01-02 to 2026-10-21 (2,968 bars, get_equity_historicals), split into close-to-open and open-to-close log returns.
- 47 NVDA earnings nights were checked against the price gaps.
- Overnight mean 2017-26, earnings excluded: +12.4bp (sd 1.70%). Intraday mean: +4.0bp.

Paths
- 20,000 paths per configuration, 252 trading days from 10/23/2026.
- Stationary block bootstrap (mean block 10 days) of (overnight, intraday) pairs from 2017-08 to 2026-10, earnings nights excluded.
- Returns rescaled to 40% annual volatility and re-centred to each scenario's drifts.
- Earnings nights (11/17, 2/24, 5/26, 8/25) drawn from the empirical earnings pool, scaled to 6% rms.

Engine model
- NVDL night return = exp(1.9 x NVDA overnight - 0.0009), i.e. 4bp tracking plus 5bp costs.
- 0.88 of engine capital invested; cash on earnings nights.
- KILL: first touch of $50 or below freezes the path.

Option model
- Black-Scholes with r = 4%.
- IV = sqrt(0.5 x RV20^2 + 0.5 x 0.40^2) x (1 + vrp), plus (5.8% x (1 + vrp))^2 earnings variance when a report falls before expiry.
- Smile fitted to the 10/22 chain: σ/σ_atm = 0.915 + 0.06(k - 1.2)^2, with k = ln(K/S)/(σ√T).
- Calibration at vrp 0.08: within about ±5% of Nov-13 and Nov-20 marks near the money. Prices Dec and Jan out-of-the-money calls 4-19% above market, which is conservative for a buyer.
- Costs: pay 50% of each leg's half-spread on entry and on exit. Half-spread = max(0.01, 0.02p + 0.01) x (1 + 6 x max(0, T - 0.15)), fitted to the Nov, Dec, Jan and Apr quotes. Plus $0.04 per contract per leg.
- P(200) is first passage of end-of-day marked equity.

Scenarios
- A: overnight +12bp/night, NVDA drift +20%/yr.
- A0_rich: drift 4% (equal to r) and IV x1.25. The sleeve's mean payoff is 0.89x per trade: the "options are fair, you pay spread and volatility premium" case.
- B: overnight +6bp, drift 15%.
- C: no edge; overnight 0, drift 10%.
- H: raw 2017-26 replay; drift about 41%/yr, vol 47%.
- X: bear; drift -30%/yr.

designs.edge_basis:
ENGINE: unchanged evidence.
- NVDA close-to-open: +12.4bp/night 2017-26 with earnings excluded (2,424 nights; sd 1.7%).
- The edge is regime-dependent: 2022 -23bp, 2025 +6bp. The 15:52-09:31 executable version measured about +20bp, t ≈ 1.0, in 2026.
- Live record: 31 nights, about -4.8%.

SLEEVE: no proven statistical edge is claimed. It is a deliberate purchase of variance and right-tail convexity. A sub-fair bet sized boldly raises the chance of reaching a far target; this is a Dubins-Savage-type effect.

Why it raises P($200):
- One 3x take-profit adds about $32 at today's equity. Two wins, or one win plus engine drift, reach $200.
- The take-profit sells convexity early: a +13-18% NVDA move within 4-6 weeks triples a +41% OTM spread through delta and vega.
- That rally frequency is 24-32% in the vol-40%, drift-20% bootstrap, 20-27% at drift 4%, and 41-51% in raw 2017-26 history.

Whether the sleeve makes money depends on NVDA's real drift exceeding the 4% option-pricing rate:
- Drift 20% (scenario A): mean payoff 1.30x per trade.
- Today's quotes priced the Nov-20 250/255 spread at about 5% implied odds of NVDA closing above ~+19% at expiry. The comparable 20-day rally frequency is 10.6% in raw 2017-26 history, 5.3% after the base-scenario rescale, and 5.1% in 2025-26. So options look cheap only if the 2017-26 mega-trend repeats.
- With fair or rich options (A0_rich): mean payoff 0.89x per trade.

Costs:
- The floor bounds the cost: at most about $17 of today's capital can be lost to the sleeve before it switches off at E < $88.
- The cost shows up as a lower median (scenario A: $98 vs $135 at 12 months), P(end below start) of 50% vs 20%, and 5-12 points more KILL risk.
- Weekly log growth is lower in every scenario except the raw-history replay H.

Evidence quality is low to moderate:
- Model calibrated to a single day's chain.
- Bootstrap from one stock's bull decade, which keeps that decade's fat right tail even after demeaning.
- Results are very sensitive to the drift assumption.
risks: Median outcome gets worse. Scenario A: median 12m equity $98 vs $135 engine alone; P(end below $97.30) 50% vs 20%. In the fair-options case the median is $90 and expected log growth falls from +0.61%/week to +0.08%/week.
KILL risk rises. P(touch $50 within 12m): A 8.0% vs 2.9%; half-edge B 15.9% vs 7.0%; no-edge C 28.6% vs 16.8%; bear X 35.8% vs 20.8%.

Everything is NVDA. The engine (NVDL/NVDX) and the sleeve (NVDA spreads) fail together in an NVDA drawdown. The floor caps the sleeve's loss, but the engine has no stop and can gap -20% in one night at full size.

The sleeve's value depends on the drift assumption. With options fairly priced (A0_rich, mean payoff 0.89x) P(>=200) rises only from 19% to 24% while KILL risk triples. The positive sleeve EV in scenario A comes from assuming +20%/yr NVDA drift against 4% option pricing.

Model risk. Black-Scholes with a smile fitted on one day (10/22, after a -4.4% NVDA day). The bootstrap keeps 2017-26's fat right tail, which may make out-of-the-money spreads look cheaper than they are. Flat-IV and earnings-crush dynamics are simplified, and the take-profit is checked on daily closes only.

Execution and liquidity. Far out-of-the-money legs have wide markets: Jan-15 310C 0.30/0.38 against a spread mid of 0.14, so paying natural instead of mid costs about 35% of the debit. 6-month wings are illiquid (Apr-16 340C 0.64/1.29). A 2-leg order may not fill at the limit, and a take-profit exit after a rally sells near the natural bid.

Whole-contract and whole-share lumpiness. At E ≈ $97 the sleeve is one contract (about 17% of E). The engine then holds only 2 NVDL (about 64% of E), below the 0.88 exposure the simulation assumed, which slightly overstates engine growth at the start.

Expected losing streaks. About 60-68% of cycles expire near zero, so 3-4 consecutive losers are likely. After one loss at today's equity the sleeve switches off (E < $88) until the engine recovers, which can make the strategy feel like it has stalled.
Level 3 approval may be delayed or denied (human action needed). Until it arrives, only the Level 2 fallback (long call 65% out of the money) or the engine alone is available.

Operational risk in multi-leg orders: wrong strike, expiry, side or open/close flag. Orders must be reviewed and their legs verified before sending, and INV-9 (never two live orders per symbol) applies. Short-leg early assignment is negligible (NVDA pays a $0.01 dividend), and positions are always closed 25 days before expiry.

Behavioural risk. A visible equity spike after a take-profit followed by give-back can trigger PAUSE unless the high-water uses the spread at cost, as rule S7 requires. The human may also be tempted to raise f or remove the floor; without a floor, f ≥ 0.15 gives 20-54% KILL risk in scenario A.
designs.ops_feasibility:
PDT
- Zero day trades. Spreads are opened and closed on different sessions (S5 forbids same-day closes), and the engine trade is overnight.
- All 3 PDT slots stay reserved for §7 emergencies.

Wakes and loop
- No new crons are needed. Sleeve actions run inside the existing always-on 8-minute loop between 10:00 and 15:30 ET: entry re-pricing, take-profit checks (one get_option_quotes call for 2 legs per scan) and roll orders.
- The 15:48-15:58 engine entry and the 09:26-09:33 exit keep priority.
- Overnight news cannot be reacted to. This is acceptable because the sleeve's maximum loss is its debit and there is no stop.
- About 6 roll dates per year are pre-computed (first 12/21/2026), plus one open after Level 3 approval.

Liquidity at our size (1 contract)
- NVDA options are the most liquid single-stock chain. Jan-15 300C open interest 68,196 (0.47/0.49); 310C 15,065 (0.30/0.38).
- Near-money monthly spreads are 1-5% of premium. Far out-of-the-money 3-month spreads cost 25-35% of the debit from mid to natural, which the rule handles with mid + 25% limits and patient $0.01 steps.
- 6-month wings were rejected as illiquid.
- NVDL and SOXL options were rejected: NVDL Nov-20 40C 0.40/0.65; SOXL Nov-20 130C 1.30/2.25 (post-close quotes).

Fees and ticks
- About $0.03-0.05 per contract per leg; $0.01 ticks below $3.00.

Cash
- A debit spread in a limited-margin account needs only the debit. Proceeds are usable immediately for the 15:52 engine entry.

Fills
- Expect most entries within 1-3 scans at mid + 0.01 to 0.03.
- If not filled by 15:30, the order is cancelled and retried the next day (at most 3 days).

Records and reviews
- New trades.csv kinds and a state.sleeve block. Reviews are process-only at 2027-01-11, with P&L judged after 6 cycles.

Live examples are read-only
- No orders were placed and no account-changing tools were called in this research.

0. SCOPE

- Holidays: the spread is entered on the last trading day of the week and expires on the first trading day of the next week.

  - Thu 12/24 is a half day, then a holiday: entry 12/24 at 12:50 for Monday 12/28; no NVDL that Thursday.
  - 12/31: entry 15:50 for Monday 1/4; no NVDL that night.

2. INSTRUMENT
- SPY puts expiring on the next trading day (normally Monday).
- Sell put K_s and buy put K_s-1 as ONE 2-leg limit order for a net credit.
- SPY only. XSP, QQQ, NVDA and iron condors were rejected (see live_examples).

3. FRIDAY 15:45 CHECKS
Data: SPY quote, the VIX index quote (id 3b912aa2-88f9-4682-8ae3-e39520bdf4db), then get_option_instruments by strike_price and get_option_quotes for the Monday expiry.
(a) Richness filter.
- sigV = VIX/100/sqrt(252).
- K_a = the strike nearest S. T = mid(put K_a) + mid(call K_a).
- m = T / (0.798 x S x sigV). Trade only if m >= 0.75.
- Equivalently, T >= 0.5985 x S x sigV. With S=764 and VIX 19.03 that is T >= $5.48. Today's 1-day straddle was 5.48, so m = 0.750.
- The filter blocks trades when the market prices short-dated vol cheaply. On 10/21's closing marks the curve was about 0.8-0.94 of today's, and at that level the per-trade EV is negative.
(b) Short strike.
- K_s = the put with |delta| closest to 0.20.
- It must also satisfy S - K_s >= 0.6 x sigV x S (about $5.5 today). If the 0.20-delta strike is closer than that, use the highest strike that meets the distance.
- Long leg = K_s - 1.
(c) Credit floor: C = mid(K_s) - mid(K_s-1) must be >= $0.14.
(d) Size: always exactly 1 contract. ML = 100 - 100 x expected fill credit.
- Need E - 3 >= ML, with E = cash after the 09:31 exit.
- If not, try strikes upward one at a time while |delta| <= 0.30 (ML about $75-78).
- If no strike qualifies, the options leg is OVER. Revert permanently to RULES_v3 (5-night NVDL) with the remaining equity.
(e) If any check fails: skip that weekend and hold cash Fri 15:52 to Mon.
- Every Friday, traded or not, write a shadow line to state: S, VIX, T, m, K_s, delta, C, natural credit.

4. ORDER MECHANICS (Friday)
- 15:50:00 limit credit = mid, rounded to the cent (round 0.005 up).
- 15:53: cancel and replace at mid - 0.01.
- 15:56: mid - 0.02, never below max($0.14, natural).
- 15:59: if still unfilled, cancel, VERIFY the cancel, and skip the weekend.
- Never more than one live option order.
- Records: trades.csv exit_kind "wps"; orders.jsonl intent line (INV-12).

5. MONDAY (expiry day; Robinhood's sellout time is 15:45 ET)
- No stop-loss before 15:30; the risk is already defined.
- 15:35 and 15:40: if SPY last <= K_s + 1.00, buy to close.
  - Limit at mid + 0.01; after 60 s, natural; after 120 s, up to $1.00.
  - This is not a day trade, because the position was opened Friday.
- 15:55 final check: if the position is still open and SPY <= K_s + 0.30, close at natural or market immediately.
- Otherwise let it expire worthless (no closing cost).
- If Robinhood sells out only the short leg, sell the remaining long leg the same day.
- Never carry a short SPY put within $0.30 of the money into 16:00.

6. TARGET, KILL, PAUSE
- TARGET: the first EOD mark with E >= $200 stops all new spreads and NVDL entries. Alert the human ("target reached") and hold cash until the human instructs.
- KILL (RULES §6, unchanged): E <= $50 means flatten, HALT, alert the human. One max loss from about $97 lands at about $12-16, so one bad weekend ends the campaign.
- PAUSE §6 does not apply to the spread (1 lot is the minimum). NVDL nights keep §6 sizing.
- Never use a second contract. The 2-contract variant raised P(<= $20) by about 4-5 points with no gain in P(>= $200).

7. IDLE CASH
- Cash.
- The credit received is buying power, but it is part of the spread's margin; do not spend it.

8. PRE-REGISTERED REVIEW
- Due at 12 traded weekends or on 2027-01-11, whichever comes first.
- Stop permanently if realized mean P&L per spread is below 0 after 12 trades.
- Never relax m >= 0.75 or the delta and distance rules after a winning streak.
- If more than 80% of Fridays fail the filter, report that the leg is mostly idle (in that case the plan approximates the baseline minus the weekend and Monday nights).

designs.edge_basis:
The design rests on three edges. None is proven at our size, and all three are worth far less than the variance the strategy carries.

(1) Variance risk premium on SPY 1-day puts.
- At today's prices, delta-0.20 $1 put spreads cost about $0.17 at mid. The VIX-normalized historical payoff (2012-2026) is about $0.14 (all regimes) or about $0.154 (VIX 17-21 regime, unnormalized).
- That leaves a gross edge of about $1.6-3.1 per spread at mid. After a $0.01 fill haircut and fees it is about +$0.5 to +$2.
- This is one snapshot taken after a -1.2% day. Yesterday's calm-day closing marks priced the same expiry at about 0.8-0.94 of today's VIX-normalized level, where EV is negative.
- Hence the m >= 0.75 richness filter: trade only when the market charges at least today's price.

(2) Weekend effect: options are overpriced over non-trading days.
- Jones & Shemesh, Journal of Finance 2018; related overnight findings in Muravyev & Ni, JFE 2020.
- Today's chain prices Friday-to-Monday at about 1.31x a weekday's variance (10/26 vs 10/23 ATM straddles). Realized Friday-to-Monday SPY variance, VIX-normalized, was 0.97x a weekday (n = 672 vs 2,910).
- This is the reason to sell only on Fridays. The implied side is a single observation; the Friday shadow log will measure it.

(3) Positive equity drift helps put sellers.
- I keep only half of 2012-2026's drift in the central case and none in the pessimistic case.

Evidence quality is LOW to MODERATE.
- The real-world side has 14 years of data, but the market side is one day, and edge per trade is about 2-4% of risk with a model uncertainty of plus or minus that much.
- Crucially, even with the edge, 1 contract at $97 is far above Kelly, so expected log growth is negative in every scenario (-0.004 to -0.05 per week).
- The design does not make money in expectation of log wealth. It raises the probability of reaching $200 quickly, at the price of about a 1-in-7 chance of ending at or below $20.
- If the human's goal is "best odds of $200 soon, accepting a high chance of losing most of it", this is the cleanest premium-selling way to do it. If losing the $97 matters, the baseline is better whenever its NVDA edge is real.
risks: Max loss of about $84 (87% of equity) on about 12-16% of traded weekends. One max loss from about $97 leaves about $12-16, which triggers KILL ($50) and ends the campaign. There were 2-9 full-loss Fridays per year in 2017-2026, clustered in 2018, 2020 and 2022.
Negative expected log growth in every scenario: 1 lot is 4-30x Kelly, and per-trade E[log] at $97 is -0.12 to -0.23. The median outcome is bimodal: either locked at $200 or busted.

Model risk: the edge depends on how richly the market prices short-dated SPY vol (lam). I calibrated on one post-selloff snapshot. Calm-day prices (10/21) implied lam of about 0.8-0.94, where EV is -$1 to -$2 per trade. The filter may then block about 50-97% of Fridays, so the leg could rarely trade.
The weekend overpricing (1.31x implied vs 0.97x realized) comes from a single Thursday observation. Friday-afternoon pricing of the Monday expiry may differ.

Pin and assignment risk: SPY options are American-style and physically settled. If SPY finishes between the strikes after the 15:40/15:55 checks, assignment of 100 SPY (about $76k notional) in a $97 limited-margin account means an overnight gap could exceed the defined risk. This is mitigated by the 15:35, 15:40 and 15:55 closes and Robinhood's 15:45 sellout, but not zero. XSP would remove it but costs about the whole edge in fills.

Execution: no fill means a skipped weekend. Natural is $0.02-0.03 below mid, and each $0.01 is about $1, roughly 30-70% of the expected edge. Robinhood's regulatory fees are assumed at $0.04 per contract per leg.
Weekend gaps cannot be reacted to (Robinhood equity options trade 09:30-16:00 only). Loss is capped at the width, but a gap below K_s-1 on Monday morning means a certain max loss.
Collateral timing: if Robinhood does not release the Monday spread's buying power before Tuesday 15:52, that NVDL night is reduced or skipped.
Level 3 may be denied or delayed. The fallback is the unchanged baseline.

The baseline-comparison numbers use heuristic NVDA earnings nights (a couple were mapped to the wrong night) and 2017-2026 history only. NVDA overnight edge decay (RULES §3(f)) also lowers the hybrid's Tue-Thu contribution.
Interaction with existing rules: one losing weekend can trip KILL and PAUSE thresholds designed for a 2x ETF. The human must accept that a single trade can end the campaign.

designs.edge_basis:
Weak but real-looking; the main effect is variance, not edge.

(1) Options by themselves lose money for buyers here. Always-on weekly NVDA or SPY ATM spreads and calls lose -7% to -30% per bet across drift scenarios: the skew makes call spreads cost 0.55-0.60 per $1 against an N(d2) of about 0.49, and implied vol exceeds realized (NVDA IV 40% vs RV 29-36%; SPY 16.4% vs 10-11%; QQQ 30% vs 18%). Far-OTM weeklies are worse.

(2) The only signal I found that survives: short-term reversal in an uptrend, RSI(2) < 10 with price above the 200-day average. This is Connors' rule, published in 2008, so 2009-2026 is out-of-sample for it. On SPY 2016-2026: 5-day forward mean +0.51%, P(up) 0.67 (157 signal days), vs unconditional 0.61. 2021-26: P(up5) 0.68, mean +0.89%. Expressed as a $1 ATM call spread, that is +5% to +16% per bet after modeled costs. The t-statistic is about 0.6-2.2 depending on the drift assumption, and the edge is positive in both sub-periods only if equity drift persists. In the bootstrap it dilutes to about 0 (-7% to +4%). Signals cluster in sell-offs: Feb 2025 lost 4 straight; Mar 2026 lost 2; Jul 2025 and Jul 2026 lost too.

(3) The core's overnight drift is the only other measured edge (NVDA close-to-open +20bp/night in the last year, t about 1), and it does not transfer to calls (see live_examples).

Net: the overlay's expected value per bet is somewhere between -7% and +16%. At a forced 58%-of-equity size its expected log growth is negative even at the historical win rate. It raises P($200) mainly by converting KILL probability into target probability.
risks: First-loss ruin: at E about $97, one losing spread (-$56) leaves about $40, below the $50 KILL, and the campaign halts. Historical P(first bet loses) is about 30-40%; market-implied about 42-45%.

The edge may be zero: per-bet EV ranges from -7% (bootstrap, no drift) to +16% (real path). It is a published rule that weakens if trend or drift fades; a bear market switches it off only through the SMA200 filter, after the damage starts.
Signal clustering: in sell-offs RSI2<10 fires repeatedly (Feb 2025: 4 straight losers; Mar 2026: 2), and the NVDL core is long NVDA the same nights, so losses are correlated.
Position size is 2-4x Kelly at today's equity (minimum lot about $56 = 58% of E). Expected log growth is negative and the median ending equity falls to about $50 in the planning case.
Execution: 15:50 combo fills may be 2-6 cents worse than mid. At $0.06 per side the per-bet EV drops by about 6 points and P(touch 200) falls from about 33% to about 29%.

Expiry-day mechanics: pin risk around K1/K2, the Robinhood forced close at 15:45, a missed 15:30 bridge, early assignment of the short leg near a SPY ex-dividend date (avoid holding through it; next about 12/18), and half-day expiries (11/27, 12/24).
Level 3 may be denied or delayed (then the L2 fallback is core only), or approval could come with restrictions on 1-wide spreads.

Model risk: Black-Scholes pricing with realized-vol-based IV and a skew calibrated on a single stress day (10/22). The bootstrap breaks some reversal structure; the replay has only about 9 independent years, and NVDA's history carries hindsight bias in the H scenario.
Behavioral risk: deviating after a loss (doubling to 'get back') would turn the plan into the all-in variant (P(end <= $20) about 15%).

Wake schedule: uses the existing 15:48 ENTRY wake. Bridge to 15:50:00 for the signal (SPY last + stored closes), order at 15:50:30, re-price 15:53:30, cancel 15:57:00, NVDL entry 15:52 sized on cash minus $65 reserved. Cash: a limited-margin account must hold the full debit (about $56-62). The rest of equity (about $35-40 at E=$97, i.e. 1 NVDL share) runs the core. Fees: $0 commission, about $0.05-0.10 regulatory per spread round trip.

Frequency: about 14.6 signal days per year historically (about 9 non-overlapping trades). In practice about 2 bets are placed before the plan retires at $200 or hits KILL.

Prerequisites: L3 approval on 8334; a SPY daily-close history file for RSI2/SMA200 (Robinhood daily bars back to 2015); a stored list of SPY ex-dividend dates; trades.csv rows of kind "spr".

judgements.best_combination:
Adopt D3 (Floor-Funded Barbell) on the unchanged NVDL engine, with two amendments, and nothing else on top.

(1) Lock at $200. At the first scan where cash plus the spread's liquidation value (mid minus 25% of the leg half-spreads, minus fees) is >= $200, close the spread, place no new risk and alert the human. Without this rule D3's P(200) is only first passage of marked equity.

(2) Keep D3's sizing: floor F = $80 (fixed), B = min(0.20E, E - 80), one 3-month $10-wide NVDA call debit spread, take profit at 3x the debit, roll at 25 DTE, skip the cycle when B < $8.

First trade after Level 3 approval: BUY 1 NVDA 2027-01-15 300C / SELL 1 2027-01-15 310C, net debit limit <= $0.16 (live 10/22: 0.47/0.49 and 0.30/0.38; mid 0.14, natural 0.19; max loss about $16.10).

P(<=50) is 8-10% vs 3-5%, median $87-98 vs $130, and log growth is +0.0 to +0.35%/wk vs about +0.5%/wk.

Do NOT add D2's earnings spread on top. In my shared-budget hybrid it raised 12-month P(<=50) from about 8% to 17-18% for roughly -1 to +2 points of P(200).

If only Level 2 is granted: keep the baseline, or use D3's single-call fallback (1 Jan-15 350C at <= $0.12). I did not independently verify that fallback.

Reject D4, D5 and D1 while the account cannot be refilled. D4 maximizes P(200) at about 50%, but carries about 15% P(<=$20). D5 has 35-52% P(<=50). D1 is no better than the baseline and has 36-40% P(<=50).

plan.dissent:
1) "No lock, so the headline P(200) is only first passage" (all three judges).
- FIXED with rule R6(b). The lock fires on liquidation value with the spread at natural, and the sim values the spread at bid.
- Odds are reported both at period end and as "reached".

2) "It buys variance, not edge: lower median, lower log growth, half of paths end below start; positive EV only if NVDA drift beats the ~4% rate options price in" (J-quant, J-skeptic).
- Accepted and stated plainly to the human:
  - median $95 vs $135;
  - +0.47 vs +0.61%/week;
  - about 50% of paths end below $97.
- The cost is bounded: about $17 is at risk now, and the sleeve sleeps below $88.
- My rerun shows the P($200) lift survives the stresses:
  - options rich vs realized: 19.7% vs 7.9% at end;
  - drift = r with IV 15% rich: 17.7% vs 13.8%;
  - no edge: 9.1% vs 0.5%.
- Its price is +3 to +12 points of KILL risk.

3) "Everything rides on NVDA; a 2022-like path kills both" (J-skeptic: about 86% KILL either way).
- Accepted. The §3(f) edge-decay switch is the only defence. No uncorrelated edge was found to diversify into.

4) Whole-share lumpiness (J-ops).
- At E about 97 a $16 ticket cuts the engine from 3 to 2 NVDL (about 96% to 65% exposure).
- That gives up roughly $2-4 of expected engine gain per cycle at today's size, which the sim (0.88 exposure for both) does not capture.
- Accepted as a known cost.

5) Wide far legs (J-ops).
- The Jan-15 310C is 0.30/0.38 against a spread mid of 0.14; Feb-19 far strikes were 0.40/0.96 at the close.
- Mitigations:
  - mid + 25% limits, +$0.01 steps, a budget cap;
  - the R4 liquidity guard;
  - DTE >= 70, which keeps the very liquid Jan-15 expiry through 11/6;
  - shadow quotes before going live.

6) Tooling: multi-leg orders are limit-only, need a user-approved net price, and pre-trade alerts need acknowledgement (J-ops).
- review_option_order runs before every order.
- The human's approval of this plan is the one-time OK for the rule-based limit.
- Alerts defer the order to the next session; the 10:00-15:30 window absorbs this.

7) "Too timid for big gains" (the human's likely objection).
- Bolder designs were scored and rejected because the account cannot be refilled:
  - D4 (weekend SPY put spreads): about 50% P(200), but about 15% P(<=$20) and negative log growth. Its weekend-premium evidence was overstated: 1.13x, not 1.31x.
  - D5 (dip spreads): 35-52% KILL.
  - D1 (all-in nightly calls): no better 12-month P(200) than the baseline, with 36-40% P(<=50).
  - D2 (earnings spread): about +12 points of P(200) for about +13 points of P(<=50). Its edge is hindsight-heavy: 0.56x payoff over the last 8 reports.
- The $70-floor dial adds about 2 points of P(200) for about 4.4 points of KILL.

8) D2 as a later add-on.
- J-ops is in favour; J-quant and J-skeptic are against: shared-budget tests raised P(<=50) from about 8% to 17-18%.
- Resolved as "not now; quarterly review only, E >= $130, shared cap".

9) Model risk.
- The smile is calibrated on one post-selloff day, and the bootstrap draws from NVDA's bull decade.
- The model prices our spread about 20% above market, i.e. conservatively.
- The shadow log and the process-only first review are the checks.

10) The Level-2 fallback is model-fragile (J-skeptic).
- Its downside is identical (the same floor-funded budget of about $12-17), so it runs by default in L2-only mode. The human can veto it.
